Doug DeMuro Sold His Ford GT To Buy a Ford GT
8 photos
Photo: Doug DeMuro | YouTube
Doug DeMuro said he would do it. It was his plan right from the get-go. The sole reason for selling his Ford GT was to buy another Ford GT. Now here he is, showing his new car on camera. After eight years of owning a blue Ford GT, he now owns another blue Ford GT. And no, they aren't much alike.
The YouTuber bought the 2005 Ford GT in Midnight Blue from its original owner, automotive journalist Karl Brauer, eight years ago. Brauer had kept an impressive logbook where he documented every single event from his car’s life, even tracking every single fuel stop.
He chose it because it was basically the only Ford GT that he could afford at the time. Why was it cheaper than the rest? It had roughly 31,000 miles on the clock, which is a massive number for a collector car.
Unlike most supercar owners, Doug DeMuro didn't park it in a climate-controlled garage, hoping to cash in one day. He drove the wheels off it, adding 14,400 miles (23,175 kilometers) and pushing the total mileage to a whopping 45,800 miles (73,708 kilometers).
Photo: Doug DeMuro | YouTube His former Ford GT is powered by the hand-assembled 330-cubic-inch (5.4-liter) V8 with four valves per cylinder and an Eaton 2300 Lysholm supercharger. The setup pumps out 550 horsepower (558 metric horsepower) and 500 pound-feet (678 Newton meters) of torque.
Those are enough to make it flash from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in just 3.3 seconds and max out at 205 mph (330 mph). A six-speed Ricardo manual transmission sends power to the tarmac through the rear wheels.
DeMuro listed his car on his own platform, "Cars and Bids," with no reserve. After a week spent online, it went home with the one who placed the most generous offer: $540,000. The seller announced that what he gets from the buyer of his old Ford GT will fund a big portion of his new Ford GT.
Because it was a true driver’s car, it wore its history openly, as the listing disclosed rock chips on the nose, marks on the paint protection film, some clearcoat failure on one wheel, along with wear on the seats and scratches on the shift knob.
Photo: Doug DeMuro | YouTube Roughly three weeks later, here he is, showing up on camera to brag about his 2006 Ford GT Heritage Edition . Yes, "Heritage Edition" is the key here. Because he acquired the car through a private sale rather than a public auction block, the final transaction price remains confidential.
But just to get an idea about the potential price, this exact car sold publicly back in 2023 at the Barrett-Jackson 2023 Scottsdale Auction for $594,000, which is $54,000 over what DeMuro got for his former Ford GT. At the time, it had only 3,460 miles on the clock.
Thousands of miles were added in the meantime, all the way to 19,000 miles. In the very strict collector world, a high-mileage Heritage Edition drops significantly from the $1.5 million to $2.1 million prices commanded by sub-1,000-mile cars.
Higher-mileage Heritage Edition examples sit right around the $750,000 to $850,000 range on the used car market. With a high-mileage Ford GT Heritage Edition, Doug can now drive his new supercar guilt-free. The car belonged to Grammy-winning musician John Mayer.
Photo: Doug DeMuro | YouTube
Doug DeMuro’s new 2006 Ford GT Heritage Edition is one of only 343 units ever built. It is finished in the world-famous and ultra-popular Gulf Oil light blue and Epic Orange , paying tribute to the legendary Ford GT40 that won the 24 Hours of Le Mans back-to-back in 1968 and 1969.
The amusing part of it is that a few years ago, Doug DeMuro said that, with this livery, the Ford GT Heritage Edition looked like a clown. Well, now he owns a "clown."
Why did Doug DeMuro make the switch? Well, first, the Ford GT Heritage Edition is his all-time dream car, along with the Porsche Carrera GT, which he has owned for three years, and the Lamborghini Countach , which was first parked in his garage four years ago.
Despite owning the 2005 Ford GT for eight years, which is longer than any of the cars he has owned so far, Doug says he has never actually liked the color. In the meantime, the Midnight Blue gained traction among collectors, as blue with white stripes is one of the most sought-after combos.
Photo: Doug DeMuro | YouTube Furthermore, it was a good moment to sell his Ford GT. Over the last eight years, the collector market shifted dramatically, with prices going through the roof. So, it was the right time to cash in and use the money to buy a Ford GT that he actually liked the color of.
As for performance, the 2006 Ford GT Heritage Edition is a Ford GT is basically a standard Ford GT underneath, sporting the same engine, horsepower, torque, 0 to 60 time, and top speed.
